independent_variables.name: FEStreet
independent_variables.definition: Street-based quarterly forecast error: I/B/E/S Street reported EPS minus the median consensus EPS forecast for the final month of the fiscal quarter, divided by stock price from that final month. I/B/E/S Street actual EPS reflects a continued-operations basis; it excludes extraordinary items, discontinued operations, and other non-operating items and is adjusted to match analyst forecasts. The paper describes additional exclusions only generally as certain nonrecurring charges, without a complete charge-level screen.

evidence.quote: We define quarterly forecast errors as reported earnings minus median consensus forecasted earnings, scaled by stock price (all data from the last month of the fiscal quarter). We calculate two different forecast errors using the two reported earnings per share measures, EPSGAAP and EPSStreet, and we denote the forecast errors as FEGAAP and FEStreet.
I/B/E/S earnings per share (“EPSStreet”) reflect a company’s earnings per share reported on a “continued operations” basis.

Thus, like our GAAP measure of net income, the I/B/E/S definition also excludes extraordinary items and earnings from discontinued operations. But in addition, it also excludes “other non-operating items.”
Street earnings are obtained from I/B/E/S and reflect GAAP earnings per share adjusted for certain charges considered by I/B/E/S to be nonrecurring.

research_interest_evidence.quote: P2 : Stock returns are more highly associated with Street earnings than with GAAP earnings.

Thus, overall it appears that investors are displaying an increasing preference for EPSStreet over EPSGAAP, despite the fact that EPSStreet excludes an increasing proportion of expenses required under GAAP.

independent_variables.research_interest_reason: FEStreet is one of the two forecast-error measures whose return association is tested under the paper’s Street-versus-GAAP prediction.

independent_variables.name: FEGAAP
independent_variables.definition: GAAP-based quarterly forecast error: Compustat GAAP EPS minus the median consensus EPS forecast for the final month of the fiscal quarter, divided by stock price from that final month. GAAP EPS is income before extraordinary items and discontinued operations per average common shares outstanding adjusted for stock splits. The Data section identifies income as item #8, while the Table 1 note says item #25; the item-code conflict remains unresolved.

evidence.quote: We define quarterly forecast errors as reported earnings minus median consensus forecasted earnings, scaled by stock price (all data from the last month of the fiscal quarter). We calculate two different forecast errors using the two reported earnings per share measures, EPSGAAP and EPSStreet, and we denote the forecast errors as FEGAAP and FEStreet.

GAAP earnings per share from Compustat (“EPSGAAP”) reflect income before extraordinary items (quarterly data item #8) divided by the average common shares outstanding during the quarter (data item #61) adjusted for stock splits (data item #17).

GAAP earnings are obtained from Compustat and are defined as earnings before extraordinary items and discontinued operations (item #25) divided by average common shares outstanding (item #61) adjusted for stock splits (item #17).

estimation_procedure.description: Pooled firm-quarter regression of long-window buy-and-hold returns. Model 3 jointly includes FEStreet and FEGAAP and interacts each with POST92 so each earnings-error slope can differ after 1991. The authors test equality of the two pre-1992 slopes (α2=α4) and of the post-1992 total slopes (α2+α3=α4+α5); no repeated-fit grouping is reported.

review_notes: Source-first selection: the paper's P2 asks whether stock returns are more highly associated with Street earnings than GAAP earnings. Retain Table 1 Model 3, the full joint long-window-return regression with both forecast errors and both POST92 interactions; exclude one-measure comparators and the distinct trend, special-item, and earnings-release questions.

The Data section uses quarterly Compustat item #8 for GAAP income, while the Table 1 note uses item #25; the underlying earnings definition is otherwise consistent, and the item-code discrepancy is retained.

The paper states a 1985–1997 sample, says it begins in 1986 due to I/B/E/S coverage, and reports 1985 observations; Table 1 explicitly gives 1985–1997 and N=98,647 for the retained return fit. Preserve that source inconsistency.
The estimator and standard-error method are not identified. The Street actual EPS definition is described as adjusted for certain nonrecurring charges but not fully specified at the charge level.
descriptive_reason: The assigned reading contains no numeric data-value summaries for the selected model’s retained variables (Return, POST92, FEStreet, FEStreet × POST92, FEGAAP, FEGAAP × POST92). Figure 1 plots quarterly means of EPS definitions without exact numeric values, while Table 2 summarizes annual EPS growth, a separate analysis rather than descriptives of the retained forecast-error measures or their raw input levels.

The paper gives conflicting Compustat item codes for GAAP EPS (#8 in the Data section and #25 in the Table 1 note); the base extraction preserves the conflict.
